sentences.text: It is the case of the Prosecution that the informant along with Mujeebulla Jilani have been running a Private Limited Company by name Arovana.
They have approached the accused to take their shop No.5 on rent situated at J.P.Nagara.
It was agreed that the informant has to pay rent of Rs.40,000/- per month and fixed deposit of Rs.5,00,000/-.
On 16.12.2017 they have issued a cheque of Rs.20,000/- and on 16.01.2018 a cheque of Rs.2,00,000/- and on 08.02.2019 a cheque of Rs.2,00,000/-.
They have issued a cheque of Rs.2,00,000/- on 16.02.2018.
In total they have issued cheque of Rs.5,00,000/-.
The rent Agreement was executed on 19.01.2018.
However, these accused started obstructing the business of the informant.

They were claiming extra amount as maintenance,
water usage, cleaning and for repair.
On 10.01.2019, they had been to the informant and started abusing in a filthy language.
They had been to the Police Station to lodged the information but however as the accused was a senior citizen the Police were requested to settle their dispute.
On 28.01.2019 the accused were called by the Police.
But however these accused started abusing the informant in a filthy language in the Police Station itself.
On 14.01.2019 and on 28.01.2019 they had been to their shop and damaged the company board, frame, lighting and mirror worth of Rs.2,51,000/-.
They have used filthy language and soon after the incident, the informant had been to the Police Station and lodged the information against the accused persons.
3. Based on the First Information of CW1, the crime was registered in Crime No.29/2019 at J.P.Nagar Police Station.
The accused persons were arrested and released on bail.

On completion of the investigation, the Sub-Inspector of Police of J.P.Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru City filed Police Report against the accused persons alleging that they have committed the said offences.
After taking cognizance of the said offences, the process was issued to the accused persons.
The copies of the Police Report and other prosecution papers are furnished to the accused persons under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing, since there were grounds for presuming that the accused persons have committed the offences triable by this Court, charges for the offences has been framed and read over to them in Kannada language.
They have pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
4. To prove the charges framed against the accused persons, the Prosecution has produced the oral evidence of PW1 and no documentary evidences are marked.

After completion of the prosecution evidence, for the purpose of enabling the accused persons personally to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidences of the Prosecution against them, examined the accused persons under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
They have submitted that they have no defense evidence.
5. Heard the arguments of learned Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for the accused persons.
Perused the materials available on record.

6. The points for determination are;
1. Whether prosecution has proved beyond all reasonable doubts that the accused persons have committed the offences punishable under Sections 379, 420, 427, 504, 506 and 509 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code?

7. My answers to the above points are as follows:
Point No.1 : In the Negative, Point No.2 : As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 8. POINT No.1 :- It is the case of the Prosecution that accused No.1 and 2 are the owners of the shop bearing Shop No.5 situated at J.P.Nagar, Bengaluru.
The informant had taken the said shop on rent.
The informant had paid an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- as security deposit.
But however these accused started obstructing the business of the informant for one or the other reasons.
The accused had been to the shop of the informant and abused in a filthy language.
The information was lodged and after due investigation Final Report was submitted against these accused.
9. To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW9/PW1 Karagaiah who is an Investigation Officer has deposed about the investigation conducted by him.
10. On perusal, the information was lodged during the year 2019 on the ground that these accused were used filthy language to the informant.
The case was registered for the offence punishable under Section 427, 504 and 506 of Indian Penal Code.
The accused are regular to the Court since 7 years.
My Predecessor has issued summons, warrant and proclamation to secure the witnesses.
But, in spite of even proclamation, the prosecution failed to secure the witnesses.
The Prosecution even unable to examine the informant before this Court to prove the guilt of the accused.
My Predecessor has dropped all the Prosecution witnesses after giving sufficient opportunity to secure the witnesses.
The evidence available before this Court is the only evidence of CW9 who is an Investigation Officer.
But, to corroborate the evidence of CW9, there is no evidence available before this Court to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.
11. Point No.2:

In view of the Negative findings on the above Point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDERS
Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C, the accused persons are hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 379, 420, 427, 504, 506 and 509 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
Their bail bonds and surety bonds will be canceled after appeal period.
The Material Objects seized which are found worthless are ordered to be destroyed after the appeal period.
(Typed by the Stenographer in the Court Computer on my direct dictation, printout taken, corrected and then pronounced by me in the open court on 12.03.2025)

(SAHEEL AHMED.S.KUNNIBHAVI) II ACJM, Bengaluru City.
